newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: KTM sales rise 20 pct in first 9 mths.
newsitem.headline: KTM sales rise 20 pct in first 9 mths.

text.p: Austria's sole motorbike maker KTM on Tuesday reported a 20 percent rise in group turnover to 983 million schillings for the first nine months of the 1996/97 business year.
Group sales of KTM Motorradholding AG (excluding children's motorbikes and mopeds) climbed 16 percent to 14,476, the company said in a statement.
KTM said it expected full year sales to amount to 18,000 motorbikes and group turnover of 1.2 billion schillings, compared with one billion schillings last year.
The company said it had sold 1,651 children's motorbikes since it began producing them in January 1996 and predicted the figure for the full year would be around 2,500 bikes.
KTM's second main brand Husaberg reported a 49 percent jump in sales in the first nine months to 1,107 bikes.
The company noted it was on the brink of signing a takeover contract for 80 percent of WP Suspension, a Dutch producer of suspension components.

"KTM's strategic goal is to secure and develop further the most important core markets through participations," it said, adding talks on closer cooperation were underway with an importer from France -- KTM's third biggest market.
The company forecast strong sales in the fourth quarter of its four-stroke "hard endurance" bikes, that perform as well cross-country as they do on asphalt.
The company started production of the revamped two-cylinder engine line in July this year. Orders for these bikes for 1997/1998 were 20 percent above the sales for the current year, it said.
KTM shares ended 5.00 schillings lower at 837 on Tuesday. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12257
